reasons.A: Dry, understated irony and mid-length sentences close to the passage, with a Crothers-like aphorism on vague kinship and a deadpan close ('It was shorter'), but slightly more clipped and punchline-driven than his genial drift.
reasons.B: Best catches Crothers's genial essayist stance: mock-grateful tone, playful generalizations ('there are families in which stranger things have happened'), and the reflective turn to two kinds of history, with easy, varied sentence movement true to his period diction.
reasons.D: Period-correct diction and measured irony, but the movement is stiffer and more formal, and the closing reflection is earnest and explanatory rather than whimsical.
reasons.C: Modern, repetitive 'and... and' cadence and short staccato sentences ('It arrived.') read as a twentieth-century plain style, far from Crothers's leisurely, allusive humor.
